d: When a couple decides to paint the second-storey deck on their 9-year-old home it starts falling apart. Mike and his team discover that it's rotted through and an accident waiting to happen.

A homeowner tragically dies due to mold in her lungs just weeks after working in her attic. Fearing the culprit could still be hiding in the attic, her partner contacts Mike Holmes to investigate and make the home safe for her grieving family.

Mike completely re-designs and re-engineers a bad roof for a family living on both sides of a semi-detached home. Mike and his crew get to the bottom of what's overhead and find out what happens when a roof fails to do its job.

Gabe has started about 367 new renovation projects in his home. Unfortunately he's finished zero, which means his Oakville home has no kitchen, no living room, no sink and it's missing a necessary weight-bearing wall (which he also took out).

No one will ever criticize Gardner for not being creative. Instead, they'll probably criticize his complete lack of construction skill and the insane renovations found throughout his home. He fixed his staircase balusters with hockey sticks. Yep.
Kevin and Shirley want to cut down their daily commute. They sold their house quicker than anticipated and now they're stuck in rental limbo. Enter the Property Brothers.
Barbra and Greg are ready to put down roots in a home of their own. They've finally found their ideal neighbourhood and Jonathan and Drew are determined to help.
With their three children, Debra and Dan are squeezed into a tiny urban condo. Though they'd prefer to stay in the heart of the city, it's time to find the home of their dreams.
With three kids and another one on the way, Dave and Lizzy are desperate to get out of their rental and into the home of their dreams.
